minutes.headline: Commission waived T-ball field fees, went no-dogs there for the season; skate park still awaits town attorney
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission met with no public present, heard an update from the new Recreation Director on her first survey and program ideas, and worked through several small operational items: field-use rules at Marshall Park, a vendor-fair dump tank rental, and the stalled skate-park right-of-entry agreement. The board approved waiving T-ball user fees and banning dogs from the Marshall Park T-ball field for the season, discussed funding a dump tank rental from the revolving account, and approved two sets of past minutes.

budget_items.what_was_said: The facilities director is working on a contract for beach weed treatment following field cleanups; no timeline given.

budget_items.topic: Baseball booster fundraiser for field improvements
budget_items.what_was_said: Youth/high school baseball is fundraising for a new batter's eye, mound improvements, home plate cover and improved bleacher seating; the commission has not been formally contacted yet.

The new Recreation Director was told she has a programming budget line she can spend from for supplies without prior commission approval, though it's unclear how much prior director spending left in it.
Costs beyond the programming line, such as the dump tank rental, would come from the parks revolving account rather than the programming line.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park T-ball field user fees
budget_items.what_was_said: The commission discussed and then voted to waive the per-player T-ball user fee if the youth baseball program does the field maintenance itself.

budget_items.topic: Dump tank rental for vendor fair
budget_items.what_was_said: A rental company quote for a dump tank from Saturday morning through Sunday night (covering a rain date) was given; the commission moved to fund it from the revolving account.

The skate park group's document describing their bond funding plan was reviewed by facilities, the commission chair and the town manager and found satisfactory; it now awaits incorporation into the right-of-entry agreement by town counsel.

transfers.description: Dump tank rental for the vendor fair, funded from the parks revolving account (rather than the programming budget line)

decisions.decision: The new Recreation Director will draft program policies and a vendor contract form herself, route them through the town manager for legal review, and the commission will simply affirm them rather than review the legal details itself.
The Recreation Director does not need prior commission approval to run programs or spend from her programming budget line unless she feels something needs to be run by the board.

New user groups or vendors for field rentals do not need to come back to the commission for approval as long as they meet the insurance (COI) thresholds already on file, but the Recreation Director should mention new groups in her updates.
Once the right-of-entry agreement returns from the town attorney with the skate park's bond funding document incorporated, the commission will hold a meeting and vote on it.
The Recreation Director will check in with Julie Bello on CORI requirements for volunteers rather than assume school CORIs cover town volunteering.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to waive Marshall Park T-ball user fees for the season if youth baseball does the field maintenance, and banned dogs from that field for the season.
The board also agreed the new Recreation Director can spend from her programming budget line and approve new field-rental vendors on file insurance alone, without a commission vote each time.
The skate park's right-of-entry agreement remains with the town attorney, who must incorporate the project's bond-funding document before it comes back for a commission vote.
A vendor-fair dump-tank rental, to be funded from the parks revolving account, was discussed and moved, but the vote's outcome was not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: Delegating budget and vendor-approval authority to the Recreation Director means some routine parks and recreation decisions will no longer come before the Commission as a public vote.
Marshall Park users should expect a no-dogs rule at the T-ball field for the rest of the season.
The skate park project's next step is a legal document, not a commission decision, so its timeline depends on the town attorney's office.
